**Royalty & Franchise‑Financing Restructuring Blueprint – 2026 (Turkey | Egypt | Nigeria | Indonesia | Brazil)** *(Designed to protect long‑term brand economics while cushioning franchisees from currency depreciation, hyper‑inflation, and collective‑bargaining pressure.)* --- ## 1. Strategic Principles | Principle | Why It Matters | How We Deliver It | |-----------|----------------|--------------------| | **Brand‑Economics First** | Royalty must always cover brand, marketing, R&D & future innovation | Tiered floor‑royalty + performance‑premium – ensures a guaranteed per‑unit revenue while rewarding growth. | | **Inflation‑ & Currency‑Protection** | Prevent royalty shocks that drive churn | Quarterly index‑adjustments that blend currency‑deviation and CPI, capped so franchisees stay competitive. | | **Collective‑Bargaining Transparency** | An organized franchisee voice now exists in Turkey, Egypt, Nigeria; a weak voice in Indonesia & Brazil | Dedicated councils, audit‑trail dashboards, and a shared “Royalty‑Adjustment Committee” that sits on both sides. | | **Scalable, Localised Financing** | High entry cost & volatile operating costs limit network expansion | Franchisor‑backed, sales‑linked loans + equity‑hybrid options adapted to each market’s financial culture. | | **Unified Governance** | Mixed legal environments & diverse cultural norms | One‑stop portal, regional councils, and a global compliance & treasury hub. | | **Audit‑Ready & Compliant** | Regulatory scrutiny is on the rise in all markets | Dedicated local treasury, statutory audit and real‑time digital evidence for every royalty & finance transaction. | --- ## 2. Core Royalty Architecture > **Structure = Base ( R1 ) + Variable ( R2 ) + Inflation‑/Currency‑Adjuster ( R3 )** ### 2.1 Base Royalty (R1) – Fixed, Local‑Currency % | Market | R1 % of Gross Sales | Rationale | Minimum USD Floor (if applicable) | |--------|---------------------|-----------|-------------------| | **Turkey** | **4 %** | Balanced against high depreciation | USD 750 (≈ TRY 15 000) | | **Egypt** | **3.8 %** | Reflects moderate CPI | USD 700 | | **Nigeria** | **4 %** | Compensates for 24 % inflation | USD 800 | | **Indonesia** | **3 %** | Low inflation; aligns with local cost of living | USD 600 | | **Brazil** | **3.5 %** | Medium inflation, higher brand value | USD 650 | *R1 is capped in local currency at **1.5 % of sales** (Turkey, Nigeria, Egypt) or **1 %** (Indonesia, Brazil) to protect morale.* ### 2.2 Variable Royalty (R2) – Performance‑Based Incentive | Market | Threshold ( % of Gross Sales ) | R2 % Applied to Exceeding Sales | |--------|--------------------------------|---------------------------------| | Turkey | 5 % | 2 % | | Egypt | 4.5 % | 2 % | | Nigeria | 5 % | 2 % | | Indonesia | 4 % | 1.5 % | | Brazil | 4.5 % | 2 % | *Purpose*: Captures upside from high‑performing outlets, driving franchisee ambition and giving brand high‑caliber units for marketing amplification.* ### 2.3 Inflation / Currency Adjustment (R3) – Index‑Based Add‑On 1. **Primary Index** – *Local‑Currency Peg to USD* (3‑month rolling average). 2. **Secondary Index** – *Consumer‑Price Index (CPI)* (latest monthly). 3. **Royalty Index Formula** \[ RI = \alpha \times (R_{USD} - 1) + \beta \times \frac{CPI_{t} - CPI_{\text{base}}}{CPI_{\text{base}}} \] * \(\alpha = 0.6\) (currency weight) * \(\beta = 0.4\) (inflation weight) 4. **Adjustment Frequency** – Quarterly. 5. **Cap** – **+1.5 % of sales** (markets with >25 % CPI) or **+1 %** otherwise. 6. **Floor** – 0.00 % (no negative adjustment – we never reduce the base royalty for the franchisor). *R3 is applied only to the R1 portion; R2 is **not** inflation‑adjusted to preserve the incentive.* #### Example (Turkey, Q3 2026) | Component | Calculation | Result | % of Sales | |-----------|-------------|--------|------------| | R1 (4 %) | 12 M TRY × 0.04 | 480 k TRY | 4 % | | R3 (1 % inflation + 0.2 % currency) | 480 k × 0.012 | 5.8 k TRY | 0.48 % | | R2 (2 % of excess 6 M TRY) | (12 M - 6 M) × 0.02 | 120 k TRY | 1 % | | **TOTAL** | — | **604.8 k TRY** | **5.05 %** | --- ## 3. Franchise‑Financing Architecture ### 3.1 Entry‑Fee & Lease Adjustments | Market | Standard Initial Franchise Fee (USD) | Currency‑Converted / Sign‑Up | Fee‑Reductions (if high‑inflation) | |--------|-------------------------------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------| | Turkey | 12 k | ~ 20k TRY | 20 % discount → 9.6 k USD for 2026 Q3 | | Egypt | 12 k | ~ 15k EGP | 20 % discount → 9.6 k USD | | Nigeria | 12 k | ~ 30k NGN | 20 % discount → 9.6 k USD | | Indonesia | 12 k | ~ 240k IDR | No discount | | Brazil | 12 k | ~ 60k BRL | 20 % discount → 9.6 k USD | **Alternative** – *Reduced fee + performance‑based installment:* *Franchisee pays 70 % of the fee upfront; the remaining 30 % is paid over 12 months as a flat 1 % of sales until breakeven.* ### 3.2 Franchisor‑Backed Loan (Franchisee Financing) | Component | Term | Interest (Local Currency) | Conditions | |-----------|------|---------------------------|------------| | Loan | 3 years | 5 % (converted at prevailing spot) | 30 % balance paid in Year 1; remaining balance paid via 12 monthly installments tied to quarterly sales. | | Payment Deficit | If sales fall below target, loan balance converted into increased R3 (inflation‑adjuster) for the next 12 months. | | *Benefits*: Low‑cost debt, spreads cash‑flow burden, aligns repayment with performance. ### 3.3 Equity‑Hybrid Option | Market | Equity % | R1 Reduction | Eligibility | |--------|----------|--------------|-------------| | Turkey | 5 % | 0.5 % | Units with > 2 years profit history | | Egypt | 5 % | 0.5 % | Same as above | | Nigeria | 5 % | 0.5 % | Same | | Indonesia | 0 % | — | (Low‑bargaining culture) | | Brazil | 5 % | 0.5 % | Same | *Equity stakes are *shelf‑based* – they do not require active dilution; franchisor can buy out at a pre‑agreed premium after 5 years.* ### 3.4 Group Procurement & Vendor Financing * Centralised contracts with kitchen‐equipment, POS, and logistic partners. * Franchisor arranges credit lines at preferential rates (e.g., 4 % vs market 6 %). * Bulk discount transfers 5–8 % savings directly to franchisee balances. ### 3.5 Cash‑Flow Management * Automated POS‑to‑ledger integration (monthly reconciliation). * Monthly “Royalty Snapshot” exported to franchisee portal. * Escrow for 15 % of R3 in high‑inflation markets (used as working‑capital credit line). --- ## 4. Governance & Collective‑Bargaining Integration | Governance Layer | Responsibility | Key Features | |------------------|----------------|--------------| | **Regional Franchise Council (RFC)** | 1️⃣ Spokesperson per market (franchisor), 2️⃣ Representative from each franchisee association, 3️⃣ Senior franchisor exec. | Policy updates, joint lobbying, quarterly town‑halls. | | **Royalty‑Adjustment Committee (RAC)** | 1 franchisor, 1 external economist per country, 1 independent legal. | Quarterly review of indices, α & β weights, cap adjustments. | | **Digital Transparency Portal** | Full, audit‑ready calculations for each outlet. | Real‑time royalty engine, revenue‑upload, audit trail. | | **Escrow/Reserve Fund** | 15 % of R3 in hyper‑inflation markets, held by local treasury. | Credit line for rent/stock, automatic release when sales hit breakeven threshold. | ### Collective‑Bargaining Interaction * In **Turkey** & **Nigeria** (strong associations) – councils negotiate α, β values annually (e.g., Turkey: α = 0.5, β = 0.5; Nigeria: α = 0.6, β = 0.4). * In **Egypt** & **Brazil** – markets have moderate federations; councils provide quarterly feedback; franchisor retains design authority but remains responsive. * **Indonesia** (low collective culture) – friction‑free implementation; any adjustment is handled via the RAC. --- ## 5. Implementation Roadmap – 12 Months | Phase | Timing | Actions | Deliverables | |-------|--------|---------|--------------| | **Phase 1 – Design & Alignment** | Month 1–3 | • Finalise indices & tier parameters
• Draft legal agreements
• Sign RC & RAC charters | • Royalty index model docs
• Franchise‑financing template
• Governance charter | | **Phase 2 – Pilot & Feedback** | Month 4–6 | • Roll‑out in 5 Franchised & 2 Company‑owned outlets per market
• Collect sales data, test portals
• Conduct “beta” council meetings | • Pilot performance report
• Adjust R3 caps & α/β | | **Phase 3 – Full Launch** | Month 7–9 | • Activate system for 70 % of outlets
• Publish public guidelines
• Start escrow & hedging contracts | • Global portal live
• Hedge contracts signed | | **Phase 4 – Review & Optimize** | Month 10–12 | • Quarterly KPI review
• Update indices
• Final audit & reporting | • Updated royalty index sheet
• Financing KPI summary | **Governance Cadence** * **Quarterly RAC** (index review). * **Semi‑annual RFC** (policy & collective‑bargaining alignment). * **Annual Strategic Review** (brand health, expansion plan). --- ## 6. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) | KPI | Target | Measurement | |-----|--------|-------------| | **Royalty Real‑Value Stability** | < 1 % variance from projected | Quarterly | | **Franchisee Retention** | ≥ 90 % annual hold | Annual | | **Net Franchisee Margin** | ≥ 10 % | Annual | | **Cash‑Conversion Cycle** | ≤ 45 days | Monthly | | **Inflation‑Adjustment Accumulation** | ≤ 1 % cumulative penalty | 12 month | | **Collective‑Bargaining Satisfaction** | ≥ 80 % positive | Bi‑annual survey | --- ## 7. Risk & Mitigation Matrix | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigations | |------|------------|--------|-------------| | **IMF/central bank intervention** (Turkey) | Medium | High | Rapid re‑calibration of R3; 5 % temporary fee waiver | | **Supplier disruptions** (Nigeria) | Low | Medium | Dual sourcing & buffer inventory via escrow | | **Regulatory shift** (Brazil) | Low | Medium | Dedicated local compliance team, pre‑approved audit protocol | | **Collective‑bargaining default** (Egypt) | Medium | High | Escrow reserve & contingency loan line | | **Hedging loss** (Indonesia) | Low | Low | Hedge exposure capped at 30 % of royalty base | --- ## 8. Closing Recommendation Implement the **Hybrid Royalty & Financing Blueprint** as outlined: 1. **Tiered royalty** with local‑currency base, performance premium, and quarterly inflation/currency adjustment capped to protect franchisee morale. 2. **Franchisor‑backed, sales‑linked financing** (loan + equity‑hybrid) that reduces upfront costs while retaining long‐term profitability for the franchisor. 3. **Governance bodies (RFC, RAC)** with a transparent online portal to satisfy collective‑bargaining groups and regulatory bodies. 4. **Group procurement & vendor financing** to lower operating cost and improve margins. 5. **Phased rollout** with pilots in every market, continuous KPI monitoring, and an agile adjustment loop. By layering a **fixed floor royalty** that never drops below a profitable level, a **performance‑based incentive** that keeps outlets motivated, and an **inflation‑linked safety net**, the brand preserves economics in both stable‑currency (Indonesia, Brazil, Turkey—on the low‑end) and high‑volatile markets (Nigeria, Egypt, Turkey). Financing options are tailored to local risk appetite and capital structure, ensuring franchisees can enter and grow without jeopardizing the franchisor’s cash‑flow. Implementing the above will secure **brand profitability, franchisee satisfaction, and collective‑bargaining goodwill** across all five markets.
